Stan code and data of an mvgam model

Source: R/make_stan.R
stancode.mvgam_formula.Rd

The Stan program and data list of an mvgam model. For an mvgam_formula() they are generated without fitting, as mvgam() would build them from the same arguments. For an mvgam model they are the ones the model was built with. Pass the two to rstan or cmdstanr to run the model outside mvgam. The program shows how the trend enters the linear predictor.

Usage

# S3 method for mvgam_formula
stancode(
  object,
  data,
  family = gaussian(),
  prior = NULL,
  data2 = NULL,
  sample_prior = "no",
  knots = NULL,
  drop_unused_levels = TRUE,
  backend = "rstan",
  threads = 1L,
  normalize = TRUE,
  save_model = NULL,
  silent = 1L,
  stanvars = NULL,
  validate = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for mvgam_formula
standata(
  object,
  data,
  family = gaussian(),
  prior = NULL,
  data2 = NULL,
  sample_prior = "no",
  knots = NULL,
  drop_unused_levels = TRUE,
  backend = "rstan",
  threads = 1L,
  normalize = TRUE,
  save_model = NULL,
  silent = 1L,
  stanvars = NULL,
  validate = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for mvgam
stancode(object, ...)

# S3 method for mvgam
standata(object, ...)

Arguments

object

An mvgam_formula(), or an mvgam model fitted or built with run_model = FALSE.

data

A data frame holding every variable the formulas use.

family

A description of the response distribution and link function, given as a family function, a call to one or its name. Supports most brms families, including the ordinal families (brms::cumulative(), brms::sratio(), brms::cratio(), brms::acat()). The brms families needing a separate linear predictor per response category, brms::categorical(), brms::multinomial() and brms::dirichlet(), are refused: use categ(), multi() and diri(), which take the categories in long format and share one latent structure across them. A family whose mean has to stay positive needs a link that keeps it there once a trend enters the linear predictor: pair stats::Gamma(), brms::weibull(), brms::exponential(), brms::frechet() and stats::inverse.gaussian() with link = "log". Their default links leave the mean positive only where the predictor is. A latent trend is centred near zero and reaches negative values, where the likelihood is undefined. mvgam() warns before fitting. brms::lognormal() is the exception: its mu is a log-scale location that takes any sign.

A family written inside a univariate brms::bf() is the model's family, as in brms. In a multivariate model each response may take its own family, in which case name it inside that response's brms::bf(): bf(count ~ x, family = poisson()) + bf(seen ~ x, family = bernoulli()). Passing a list of families to this argument, as brms::brm() allows, is not supported; the family belongs to the response that names it. A single family given here applies to every response that does not name one of its own. Closure-unit and multi-response families (occ(), nmix(), mvn(), mvt(), diri(), multi(), categ()) lay their data out by unit. Each models its response alone and cannot be one response of a multivariate model.

prior

A brmsprior of priors to set, from brms::prior(). get_prior.mvgam_formula() lists the classes.

data2

A named list of objects the model uses that are not variables in data, as in brms::brm().

sample_prior

"no" (the default), "yes" or "only", as in brms::brm().

knots

Optional named list of knot positions for spline terms, used by the observation and trend formulas alike.

drop_unused_levels

Logical. TRUE (the default) drops factor levels without observations.

backend

"rstan" (the default) or "cmdstanr".

threads

Number of threads within each chain. Defaults to 1.

normalize

Logical. TRUE (the default) keeps the normalising constants of the sampling statements.

save_model

File path to write the Stan program to, or NULL (the default) to write nothing.

silent

Integer verbosity, as in brms::brm(). 0 prints Stan's exceptions and progress, 1 (the default) prints progress and 2 prints nothing.

stanvars

Optional brms::stanvar() object of Stan code to add to the program, merged with the code mvgam writes for the trend.

validate

Logical. TRUE (the default) checks the program with the Stan parser.

...

For an mvgam_formula(), other arguments of mvgam(). A name mvgam() does not take is refused. For an mvgam model, unused. Anything passed is refused.

Value

stancode() returns the Stan program as a character string of class mvgamstancode, which prints line by line. standata()

returns the named list of Stan data.

See also

mvgam(), mvgam_formula(), get_prior.mvgam_formula(). methods_md() writes the same model as equations for a methods section.

Other model fitting: check_newdata(), jsdgam(), mvgam(), mvgam_data(), mvgam_formula(), mvgam_multiple(), pivot_detection_array(), pivot_species_matrix(), series_to_mvgam(), update.mvgam()

Examples

set.seed(1)
dat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 2L,
                 n_timepoints = 40L, trend_model = AR())$data_train
mf <- mvgam_formula(y ~ s(x, k = 5), trend_formula = ~ AR(p = 1))

# The program of the model, before any fitting. The trend's
# parameters carry a `_trend` suffix.
code <- stancode(mf, data = dat, family = poisson())
code
#> // Generated with mvgam 2.0.0 using brms 2.23.2
#> functions {
#>   
#> }
#> data {
#>   int<lower=1> N; // total number of observations
#>   array[N] int Y; // response variable
#>   
#>   // data for splines
#>   int Ks; // number of linear effects
#>   matrix[N, Ks] Xs; // design matrix for the linear effects
#>   
#>   // data for spline 1
#>   int nb_1; // number of bases
#>   array[nb_1] int knots_1; // number of knots
#>   
#>   // basis function matrices
#>   matrix[N, knots_1[1]] Zs_1_1;
#>   int prior_only; // should the likelihood be ignored?
#>   int<lower=1> N_trend; // total number of observations
#>   int<lower=1> N_series_trend;
#>   int<lower=1> N_lv_trend;
#>   int<lower=1> N_time_trend;
#>   array[N_time_trend, N_series_trend] int times_trend;
#>   array[N] int<lower=1, upper=N_time_trend> obs_trend_time;
#>   array[N] int<lower=1, upper=N_series_trend> obs_trend_series;
#> }
#> transformed data {
#>   matrix[N_series_trend, N_lv_trend] Z = diag_matrix(
#>                                                      rep_vector(1.0,
#>                                                                 N_lv_trend));
#>   array[N] int obs_trend_idx;
#>   for (n in 1 : N) {
#>     obs_trend_idx[n] = (obs_trend_series[n] - 1) * N_time_trend
#>                        + obs_trend_time[n];
#>   }
#> }
#> parameters {
#>   real Intercept; // temporary intercept for centered predictors
#>   vector[Ks] bs; // unpenalized spline coefficients
#>   
#>   // parameters for spline 1
#>   // standardized penalized spline coefficients
#>   vector[knots_1[1]] zs_1_1;
#>   vector<lower=0>[nb_1] sds_1; // SDs of penalized spline coefficients
#>   vector<lower=0>[N_lv_trend] sigma_trend;
#>   matrix[N_time_trend, N_lv_trend] innovations_trend;
#>   
#>   // AR coefficient parameters
#>   vector<lower=-1, upper=1>[N_lv_trend] ar1_trend;
#> }
#> transformed parameters {
#>   // penalized spline coefficients
#>   vector[knots_1[1]] s_1_1;
#>   
#>   // prior contributions to the log posterior
#>   real lprior = 0;
#>   lprior += student_t_lpdf(Intercept | 3, 1.6, 2.5);
#>   lprior += student_t_lpdf(sds_1 | 3, 0, 2.5)
#>             - 1 * student_t_lccdf(0 | 3, 0, 2.5);
#>   
#>   matrix[N_time_trend, N_lv_trend] scaled_innovations_trend;
#>   scaled_innovations_trend = diag_post_multiply(innovations_trend,
#>                                sigma_trend);
#>   matrix[N_time_trend, N_lv_trend] lv_trend;
#>   
#>   // Stationary start: the t = 1 innovation scaled to the
#>   // marginal SD sigma / sqrt(1 - ar1^2)
#>   lv_trend[1] = scaled_innovations_trend[1] ./ sqrt(1 - square(ar1_trend))';
#>   
#>   // AR dynamics
#>   for (i in 2 : N_time_trend) {
#>     for (j in 1 : N_lv_trend) {
#>       lv_trend[i, j] = ar1_trend[j] * lv_trend[i - 1, j]
#>                        + scaled_innovations_trend[i, j];
#>     }
#>   }
#>   
#>   // Each series' trend is the series' state
#>   matrix[N_time_trend, N_series_trend] trend = lv_trend;
#>   
#>   // compute penalized spline coefficients
#>   s_1_1 = sds_1[1] * zs_1_1;
#> }
#> model {
#>   // likelihood including constants
#>   if (!prior_only) {
#>     // initialize linear predictor term
#>     vector[N] mu = rep_vector(0.0, N);
#>     mu += Intercept + Xs * bs + Zs_1_1 * s_1_1;
#>     mu += to_vector(trend)[obs_trend_idx];
#>     target += poisson_log_lpmf(Y | mu);
#>   }
#>   
#>   // priors including constants
#>   target += lprior;
#>   // Shared innovation priors
#>   target += exponential_lpdf(sigma_trend | 2);
#>   target += std_normal_lpdf(to_vector(innovations_trend));
#>   // AR coefficient priors
#>   target += normal_lpdf(ar1_trend | 0, 0.5);
#>   target += std_normal_lpdf(zs_1_1);
#> }
#> generated quantities {
#>   // actual population-level intercept
#>   real b_Intercept = Intercept;
#> }
#> 

# The data passed to that program: 60 observations of 2 series
# over 30 time points
sdata <- standata(mf, data = dat, family = poisson())
sdata[c("N", "N_series_trend", "N_time_trend")]
#> $N
#> [1] 60
#> 
#> $N_series_trend
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $N_time_trend
#> [1] 30
#> 

# Next, fit the model with mvgam(), which compiles this program
